active_product_bottleneck.observation: Actual Builder repeatedly preserves >9.33 MB Office savings with exactness/read-side economics, but safe snapshot control misses create law. Run 35931494298 measured base 134.960 ms, candidate 239.212 ms, proof 52.87 ms, staging 64.70 ms, commit/retention 20.74 ms. The frozen <=1.25x Office ceiling is 168.700 ms. Even the optimistic control that deletes proof completely while leaving staging/commit unchanged is ~186.34 ms (~1.381x), still red. Therefore a fusion that merely piggybacks proof onto the existing staging representation cannot close the gate; it must also make winner construction materially cheaper. The charged mode1-only oracle retained only 5,570,902 B median, so abandoning canonical mode0 surrenders ~40.3% of the proven byte gain.
active_product_bottleneck.next_discriminator: Measure code head e57992a60490234b04149dd626eba0490b7354a2, which reuses staging-computed decoded-member identities during hidden-winner commit instead of immediately hashing the same bytes again. If that is insufficient, continue the representation-boundary move toward a bounded deflate-backed hidden candidate/winner path. Native mode0 projection remains earned debt.

process_lessons.lesson: continue-on-error step conclusion can mask underlying outcome; consume the final enforcement and artifact before declaring a gate green.
Deleting filesystem I/O is not equivalent to deleting work; measure phase internals after each intervention.
Never trade away a mutation/correctness boundary for a performance green.
A simpler already-supported representation must be fully charged before it can retire portability debt; mode1's read win did not compensate for surrendering ~40% of byte gain.

Before implementing a fusion optimization, subtract the entire removable phase from measured wall time. If the optimistic lower bound still misses the frozen gate, reopen the representation boundary instead of spending an activation on an incapable local optimum.
